newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev ends firmer at 2,660-2,720 per dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev ends firmer at 2,660-2,720 per dollar.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed between 2,660-2,720 per dollar in low interbank volume, slightly firmer from the morning's 2,740-2,750, due to higher dollar supply, dealers said.
"(Foreign currency) supply rose in the afternoon, and the lev erased the losses it suffered in the morning due to higher demand," one dealer said. The lev closed at 2,670-2,700 on Monday.
Expectations of a sharp lev fall due to fuel importers' dollar purchases did not materialise because buyers were bidding only for small volumes, probably because of a lev shortage.
But there was some underlying tension in the market because fuel importers were expected to improve lev liquidity in the next few days after fuel prices were raised sharply from today, dealers said.
"The lev may easily fall to 3,000 if the central bank does not coordinate (sales to fuel importers) with commercial banks," another dealer said.

The interim cabinet raised fuel prices by up to 178 percent on Monday to free suppliers' volumes kept in storage and alleviate a crippling fuel shortage. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
